guidance: Respect platform-safe areas, bottom sheets, keyboard behavior, and thumb reach before adding decorative chrome.
Use motion to reinforce navigation and state change, not to simulate desktop-style hover richness.
validation_checks: Verify bottom-navigation, keyboard, and sticky primary actions on small screens and tall-form flows.
Check light and dark theme readability on real-device density, not just emulator scaling.

guidance: Keep navigation transitions and list performance predictable before adding visual flourish.
Design around touch, pull-to-refresh, and interrupted session recovery rather than desktop interaction assumptions.
validation_checks: Check safe areas, modal stacking, and gesture conflicts on both compact and tall screens.
Exercise offline or slow-network states so refresh patterns and retry messaging stay clear.

guidance: Use content rhythm and section hierarchy to keep long-form product pages from collapsing into generic blocks.
Favor clear content modules and reusable section logic so brand polish does not fragment across pages.
validation_checks: Review long-form page pacing, CTA spacing, and section contrast at both desktop and tablet widths.
Check component-preview parity so marketing sections and product surfaces share the same token language.

guidance: Lean on SvelteKit's file-based routing and load functions to keep data-fetching close to the components that render it.
Use Svelte's built-in transitions and motion stores for performant, declarative animations.
validation_checks: Confirm SSR and hydration produce no layout shift on first paint.
Verify transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion.

guidance: Ship mostly static HTML and reserve client-side islands only for genuinely interactive components.
Use content collections for type-safe markdown and editorial content pipelines.
validation_checks: Confirm interactive islands hydrate only where needed to keep JS payloads minimal.
Verify Lighthouse performance stays high on content-heavy pages.

guidance: Use loaders and actions to keep data and mutations colocated with routes and progressively enhanced.
Rely on native form submissions so core flows work before JavaScript loads.
validation_checks: Confirm forms submit and validate correctly with JavaScript disabled.
Verify nested routes handle loading and error states gracefully.

guidance: Use Angular Material or the CDK to align with platform conventions and built-in accessibility.
Manage async data with RxJS and the async pipe to avoid manual subscription leaks.
validation_checks: Confirm change detection strategy avoids unnecessary re-renders on large views.
Verify components meet accessibility roles and keyboard navigation.

guidance: Lean on fine-grained signals so updates touch only the DOM nodes that actually change.
Avoid destructuring props to preserve Solid's reactivity guarantees.
validation_checks: Confirm reactive updates do not trigger full-component re-execution.
Verify SSR hydration with SolidStart produces no mismatch warnings.

guidance: Compose UI with Blade components and layouts to keep server-rendered markup DRY.
Pair with Livewire or Alpine.js for interactivity without a separate SPA build.
validation_checks: Confirm CSRF tokens are present on all form submissions.
Verify Blade components render consistently across the pages that include them.

guidance: Use Turbo Frames and Streams to deliver SPA-like updates while keeping logic on the server.
Reserve Stimulus controllers for light, targeted interactivity on top of server-rendered HTML.
validation_checks: Confirm Turbo Stream updates target the correct DOM frames without full reloads.
Verify progressive enhancement keeps core flows working without JavaScript.

guidance: Use template inheritance and includes to keep server-rendered pages consistent and maintainable.
Pair with htmx for partial updates instead of a full SPA when interactivity is light.
validation_checks: Confirm CSRF tokens are present on all form submissions.
Verify partial template responses render correctly when swapped into the page.

guidance: Follow Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and use SF Symbols and Dynamic Type for native consistency.
Build adaptive layouts with stacks and grids that respond to size classes and Dynamic Type.
validation_checks: Confirm layouts adapt to Dynamic Type and larger accessibility text sizes.
Verify dark mode and high-contrast appearances render correctly.

guidance: Use Material 3 components and dynamic color to align with Android platform conventions.
Hoist state and use remember and state holders to keep composables predictable and testable.
validation_checks: Confirm composables handle configuration changes and recomposition efficiently.
Verify touch targets and contrast meet Android accessibility guidelines.

chart_types.use_when: Show how one or more continuous values change across an ordered interval such as time.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for unordered categorical comparisons where categories have no inherent sequence.
chart_types.data_shape: One ordered x usually time, one or more continuous y series sharing the same scale.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Differentiate series with distinct line styles or direct labels rather than color alone and offer a data table fallback.

chart_types.use_when: Emphasize the magnitude of a single continuous value over an ordered interval.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when comparing several overlapping series since filled areas occlude one another.
chart_types.data_shape: One ordered x time, one continuous y rendered as a filled region from a baseline.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Maintain sufficient contrast between fill and background and label the series directly rather than relying on hue.

chart_types.use_when: Show how the composition of a total breaks down across parts while the total changes over time.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when readers must compare exact values of upper bands that lack a common baseline.
chart_types.data_shape: One ordered x time, multiple continuous y series summed into a cumulative stack.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Order bands consistently, label each band directly, and provide the underlying values in a table.

chart_types.use_when: Compare a single quantitative value across a set of discrete categories.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for continuous time trends where a line communicates change more clearly.
chart_types.data_shape: One categorical dimension, one continuous measure per category.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Start the value axis at zero and label bars with values directly so meaning does not depend on length perception alone.

chart_types.use_when: Compare a measure across categories broken down by a second grouping dimension side by side.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when groups have many sub-categories that crowd bars and harm readability.
chart_types.data_shape: One primary categorical dimension, one secondary grouping dimension, one continuous measure.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use distinct patterns plus a clear legend and consistent group order rather than color alone to separate sub-series.

chart_types.use_when: Compare totals across categories while also showing each category internal composition.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when precise comparison of non-baseline segments matters since they lack a common start.
chart_types.data_shape: One categorical dimension, multiple continuous segments summed per category.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Keep segment order consistent, label segments directly, and supply a data table for exact segment values.

chart_types.use_when: Rank or compare values across categories that have long names or many entries.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when category labels are short and few where vertical columns are more conventional.
chart_types.data_shape: One categorical dimension on the y axis, one continuous measure on the x axis.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Place readable text labels at each bar end and ensure the axis begins at zero for honest comparison.

chart_types.use_when: Compare a measure across a small set of categories or discrete time periods using vertical bars.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when category labels are long or numerous where horizontal bars read better.
chart_types.data_shape: One categorical or discrete-period dimension on the x axis, one continuous measure on the y axis.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Anchor the value axis at zero and label columns directly so comparisons do not rely solely on height.

chart_types.use_when: Reveal the frequency distribution and shape of a single continuous variable across bins.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for comparing distinct named categories which calls for a bar chart instead.
chart_types.data_shape: One continuous variable grouped into ordered equal-width bins with frequency counts.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: State bin width and units explicitly and provide the binned counts as an accessible table.

chart_types.use_when: Show how a single total divides into a few mutually exclusive parts at one point in time.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid with more than five slices or when comparing similar values where angles are hard to judge.
chart_types.data_shape: A set of categories whose continuous values sum to a meaningful 100 percent whole.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label each slice with its name and percentage directly and avoid distinguishing slices by color alone.

chart_types.use_when: Show parts of a whole while using the center hole to display the aggregate total or a key figure.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid with many slices or when exact part comparison is required since angular judgment is imprecise.
chart_types.data_shape: A set of categories summing to a whole plus an optional central summary value.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Provide direct slice labels with percentages and a table fallback rather than relying on color coding.

chart_types.use_when: Examine the relationship, correlation, or clustering between two continuous variables.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when one axis is categorical or when overplotting hides density without transparency or binning.
chart_types.data_shape: Two continuous variables mapped to x and y, one point per observation.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use distinct marker shapes plus color for categories and describe the overall trend in supporting text.

chart_types.use_when: Show the relationship between two continuous variables while encoding a third as bubble size.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when size differences are subtle or bubbles overlap heavily, obscuring the third dimension.
chart_types.data_shape: Two continuous variables for position plus a third continuous variable mapped to area.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Scale bubbles by area not radius, include a size legend, and provide exact values in a table.

chart_types.use_when: Show intensity or density of a measure across the intersection of two categorical or binned dimensions.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when precise value reading is required since color encodes magnitude only approximately.
chart_types.data_shape: Two categorical or binned dimensions forming a grid, one continuous value per cell.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use a colorblind-safe sequential scale, include a legend, and reveal cell values on focus or in a table.

chart_types.use_when: Show hierarchical part-to-whole relationships where many items must fit in a compact space by size.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when precise comparison or deep hierarchy navigation matters more than space efficiency.
chart_types.data_shape: A hierarchy of nodes each with a continuous size value, nested as parent and child rectangles.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label rectangles with name and value where space allows and provide a keyboard-navigable tree or table fallback.

chart_types.use_when: Show multi-level hierarchical composition radially where each ring is a deeper level of the tree.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for flat data or when users need exact values since outer arcs are hard to measure.
chart_types.data_shape: A hierarchy of nodes with continuous values encoded as concentric rings of angular segments.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Support keyboard drill-down, label segments on focus, and expose the hierarchy as an accessible nested list.

chart_types.use_when: Compare a few entities across several quantitative dimensions on a shared radial scale.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid with many overlapping series or unrelated axes where the shapes become unreadable.
chart_types.data_shape: Multiple comparable quantitative dimensions per entity, normalized to a common scale.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use distinct line styles per series, label each axis clearly, and offer the values in a supporting table.

chart_types.use_when: Show a single value position against a defined range, target, or threshold at a glance.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for comparing multiple metrics or showing trends where it wastes space and detail.
chart_types.data_shape: One continuous value plus a defined min, max, and optional threshold bands.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Print the numeric value and target as text and use labeled threshold zones rather than color bands alone.

chart_types.use_when: Show how a quantity progresses and drops off across the sequential stages of a process.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when stages are non-sequential or counts can increase between steps, breaking the funnel metaphor.
chart_types.data_shape: An ordered set of stages each with a count, monotonically decreasing along the process.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label each stage with its value and conversion rate as text and provide the step counts in a table.

chart_types.use_when: Show how quantities flow and split between nodes where link width encodes volume.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid with many crossing flows that create visual clutter or when precise values are critical.
chart_types.data_shape: A set of source-to-target links each with a flow magnitude across defined nodes.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label nodes and major flows with values and provide a source-target-value table as a fallback.

chart_types.use_when: Track open, high, low, and close price movements of a financial instrument over time.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for non-financial or single-value series where a line chart is simpler and clearer.
chart_types.data_shape: Per time period the open, high, low, and close values on an ordered time axis.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Pair the conventional up and down colors with directional cues and expose OHLC values as a table.

chart_types.use_when: Compare the distribution, spread, and outliers of a continuous variable across groups.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for general audiences unfamiliar with quartiles or when individual points must be seen.
chart_types.data_shape: One continuous variable summarized by min, quartiles, median, and max, optionally per category.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Annotate median and quartile values directly and explain the box-and-whisker encoding in supporting text.

chart_types.use_when: Show how a normalized metric varies across geographic regions using shaded areas.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid for raw counts that track population size or when region areas distort the perceived value.
chart_types.data_shape: Geographic region identifiers joined to one continuous normalized metric per region.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use a colorblind-safe sequential scale with a legend and provide a region-and-value table fallback.

chart_types.use_when: Show how sequential positive and negative contributions build from a starting value to an ending total.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when contributions are unordered or when a simple total comparison suffices.
chart_types.data_shape: An ordered sequence of additive and subtractive values with start and end totals.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label each step with its signed value, distinguish increases and decreases by pattern plus color, and provide a table.

chart_types.use_when: Surface one headline metric with its current value and change versus a prior period at a glance.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid when users need to compare many values or understand detailed distributions or trends.
chart_types.data_shape: One primary value plus optional delta, target, and a small trend sparkline.
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Convey direction of change with an icon and text label, not color alone, and ensure the value has sufficient contrast.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to show a single measure against a target and qualitative ranges in a compact space, such as a KPI versus goal.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when you need to compare many categories or reveal distributions rather than performance against a benchmark.
chart_types.data_shape: single measure, a target value, and two or three qualitative range bands
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Do not encode the comparative measure and ranges by color alone; add text labels for the value and target marker.

chart_types.use_when: Use it inline within text or a table cell to convey the rough trend of a metric without axes or labels.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when exact values, precise comparisons, or axis context matter to the reader.
chart_types.data_shape: a single short numeric time series
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Provide an accessible text summary or the latest value, since the tiny inline form is hard to read for low-vision users.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to plan project schedules where tasks have start and end dates, durations, and dependencies.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it for data without a time span or for simple checklists that lack scheduling.
chart_types.data_shape: tasks with start and end timestamps and optional dependency links
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Pair bar position with explicit start, end, and duration text so timing is not conveyed by length and color alone.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to reveal relationships and connectivity among entities, such as social or dependency networks.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it for strictly hierarchical data or when the node count is so high the layout becomes a hairball.
chart_types.data_shape: a set of nodes and the edges connecting them, optionally weighted
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Offer a tabular or list view of connections, since force-directed layouts are difficult to interpret without sight.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to show the volume of flows between a small set of entities arranged around a circle.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when there are many entities or when precise flow magnitudes must be read off quickly.
chart_types.data_shape: a square matrix of weighted flows between categories
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Provide the underlying flow matrix as a data table and use distinguishable, non-color-reliant labels for each arc.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to explore patterns and clusters across many numeric dimensions at once with brushing.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it for presenting conclusions to non-expert audiences or for very few dimensions.
chart_types.data_shape: multivariate records with several numeric dimensions per item
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label every axis with its range and units, and avoid relying on line color alone to distinguish brushed groups.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to compare the full distribution shape and density of a numeric variable across groups.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it with small sample sizes or for audiences unfamiliar with reading density curves.
chart_types.data_shape: one numeric variable with many observations across one or more categories
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Annotate medians and quartiles with text and ensure the mirrored density outline meets contrast against its background.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to compare how a distribution shifts across many groups or time periods using stacked overlapping density curves.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when distributions barely differ or when exact values per group are needed.
chart_types.data_shape: a numeric distribution measured across many ordered categories or time periods
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Keep clear baseline labels for each ridge and ensure overlapping fills retain enough contrast to be told apart.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to show daily values over months or years and reveal weekly and seasonal patterns at a glance.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it for sub-daily data or when precise day-to-day comparisons of magnitude are required.
chart_types.data_shape: one numeric value per calendar day over an extended date range
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Use a colorblind-safe sequential scale and expose each cell's date and exact value via tooltip or focus.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to show part-to-whole composition across two categorical dimensions, like market share by segment and region.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when precise value reading matters, since variable widths and heights make exact comparison hard.
chart_types.data_shape: two categorical dimensions with proportional values forming a full whole
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label segments directly with category and percentage, and avoid relying on color alone to separate adjacent tiles.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to highlight the direction and magnitude of change for several items between exactly two time points.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it for more than two time periods or when many lines cross into an unreadable tangle.
chart_types.data_shape: values for multiple categories measured at two points in time
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Label each line at both ends with its category and value rather than depending on a color legend.

chart_types.use_when: Use it to compare two values per category and emphasize the gap between them, such as before and after across groups.
chart_types.avoid_when: Avoid it when there are more than two values per category or when overall trend over time is the focus.
chart_types.data_shape: categories each with two numeric endpoint values
chart_types.accessibility_notes: Differentiate the two endpoints with shape as well as color and label the gap value for each category.

ux_guidelines.rule: Keep the primary navigation in the same position and order on every page.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Predictable placement lets users build spatial memory instead of relearning the menu on each screen.

ux_guidelines.rule: Indicate the current location with an active nav state and breadcrumbs in deep hierarchies.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Showing where users are reduces disorientation and supports backtracking per visibility of system status.

ux_guidelines.rule: Give users a clearly marked way to back out of any flow or undo an unwanted navigation.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Clear exits support user control and freedom and prevent users from feeling trapped per Nielsen heuristic three.

ux_guidelines.rule: Limit top-level navigation to a focused set of items and group the rest under clear labels.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Fewer first-level choices reduce decision cost and make the structure easier to scan and remember.

ux_guidelines.rule: Make the site or app logo a working link back to the home or default landing screen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Users expect this convention and rely on it as a universal reset for orientation.

ux_guidelines.rule: Validate each field inline next to it on blur, not only when the form is submitted.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Early located feedback lets users fix mistakes in context instead of hunting for errors after submit.

ux_guidelines.rule: Give every field a persistent visible label rather than relying on placeholder text alone.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Placeholders vanish on input and fail screen readers, leaving users unsure what a field expects.

ux_guidelines.rule: Group related fields together and clearly mark which fields are required or optional.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Logical grouping and explicit requirements reduce confusion and abandonment in longer forms.

ux_guidelines.rule: Preserve everything the user typed when an error occurs instead of clearing the form.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Re-entering lost data is a top frustration and a frequent cause of form abandonment.

ux_guidelines.rule: Use the correct input type and autocomplete tokens so the right keyboard and suggestions appear.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Matching input modes speeds entry, cuts typos, and reduces friction especially on mobile keyboards.

ux_guidelines.rule: Acknowledge every action with a visible response within 100ms and show a progress indicator for waits over one second.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Immediate feedback keeps the interface feeling responsive and reassures users their action registered.

ux_guidelines.rule: Require an explicit confirmation step before executing destructive or irreversible actions.
ux_guidelines.rationale: A deliberate confirmation prevents costly accidental deletions and supports error prevention.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show a clear confirmation after any action that changes state such as saving or sending.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Explicit success messaging closes the loop so users know an operation completed per visibility of system status.

ux_guidelines.rule: Display loading or skeleton states for content that takes time to fetch rather than a blank screen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Visible progress communicates that the system is working and improves perceived performance.

ux_guidelines.rule: Offer an undo option for reversible actions instead of interrupting users with a confirmation dialog.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Undo preserves flow while still protecting users from mistakes, balancing speed and safety.

ux_guidelines.rule: Give every interactive control a visible focus indicator with at least 3 to 1 contrast against its background.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Keyboard users must always see where focus is to operate the interface per WCAG 2.4.11 and 2.4.7.

ux_guidelines.rule: Maintain at least 4.5 to 1 contrast for normal text and 3 to 1 for large text against its background.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Adequate contrast keeps text legible for low-vision users and in poor lighting per WCAG 1.4.3.

ux_guidelines.rule: Make all functionality operable by keyboard alone without requiring a pointer or touch.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Many assistive technologies and motor-impaired users depend entirely on the keyboard per WCAG 2.1.1.

ux_guidelines.rule: Provide descriptive alt text for informative images and empty alt attributes for purely decorative ones.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Text alternatives let screen reader users access image meaning without noise from decoration per WCAG 1.1.1.

ux_guidelines.rule: Never use color as the only means of conveying information, status, or required action.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Color-blind and low-vision users miss meaning carried by hue alone, so pair it with text or icons per WCAG 1.4.1.

ux_guidelines.rule: Render the largest contentful element within 2.5 seconds on a representative mid-range device and connection.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Slow main content erodes trust and sharply increases bounce and abandonment rates.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reserve explicit dimensions for images, ads, and embeds so content does not shift as the page loads.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Unexpected layout shifts cause misclicks and a jarring experience, so target a CLS under 0.1.

ux_guidelines.rule: Lazy-load below-the-fold images and non-critical content so the initial view loads fast.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Deferring offscreen assets cuts initial payload and speeds up the first meaningful render.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reflect the expected result immediately for slow network operations and reconcile when the server responds.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Optimistic updates make interactions feel instant and keep users in flow during latency.

ux_guidelines.rule: Serve compressed appropriately sized images using responsive sources and modern formats.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Right-sized media is often the largest performance win and reduces data cost for users.

ux_guidelines.rule: Lead with the most important information and conclusions before supporting detail.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Users scan rather than read, so front-loaded key points get seen even by skimmers.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write in plain language at a reading level appropriate to the audience and avoid unnecessary jargon.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Clear simple wording broadens comprehension and reduces support requests.

ux_guidelines.rule: Break content into short chunks with descriptive headings, lists, and meaningful subheads.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Structured scannable content helps users locate what they need without reading everything.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write link text that describes its destination instead of generic phrases like click here.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Descriptive links aid scanning and let screen reader users understand links out of context per WCAG 2.4.4.

ux_guidelines.rule: Constrain body text to roughly 50 to 75 characters per line for comfortable reading.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Lines that are too long or too short slow reading and cause readers to lose their place.

ux_guidelines.rule: Make touch targets at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels with adequate spacing between them.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Targets below this size cause mis-taps and frustration on touchscreens per WCAG 2.5.8 and platform HIG.

ux_guidelines.rule: Place primary actions within comfortable thumb reach in the lower portion of the screen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Reachable controls reduce hand strain and speed one-handed use on larger phones.

ux_guidelines.rule: Do not hide essential actions or information behind hover since touch devices have no hover state.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Hover-dependent UI is undiscoverable and unusable on touchscreens, stranding mobile users.

ux_guidelines.rule: Ensure content reflows to a single column without horizontal scrolling down to a 320 CSS pixel width.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Reflow lets zoomed and small-screen users read content without two-dimensional scrolling per WCAG 1.4.10.

ux_guidelines.rule: Do not disable pinch-to-zoom or lock the viewport scale on mobile pages.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Blocking zoom prevents low-vision users from enlarging content they cannot otherwise read per WCAG 1.4.4.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show the total cost including taxes, shipping, and fees before asking for payment details.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Hidden costs revealed late are a leading cause of cart abandonment and broken trust.

ux_guidelines.rule: Explain what personal data you collect and why at the moment you request it.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Just-in-time transparency builds confidence and supports informed consent for sensitive inputs.

ux_guidelines.rule: Display honest security and reassurance cues near payment fields without resorting to fake urgency.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Contextual reassurance at the moment of commitment lowers anxiety and increases completion.

ux_guidelines.rule: Make cancelling or downgrading a subscription as easy as signing up with no hidden or coercive steps.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Frictionless exit builds long-term trust and is increasingly required by consumer regulations.

ux_guidelines.rule: State expected response, processing, or delivery times before the user commits.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Clear time expectations prevent uncertainty and reduce anxious follow-up and support contacts.

ux_guidelines.rule: Let users experience core value before requiring account creation where feasible.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Demonstrating value first lifts conversion and reduces drop-off at the signup wall.

ux_guidelines.rule: Ask only for what is essential to start and defer non-critical setup until it is needed.
ux_guidelines.rationale: A short path to first success shortens time to value and prevents early abandonment.

ux_guidelines.rule: Surface guidance contextually at the moment of need rather than front-loading a long upfront tour.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Just-in-time tips are acted on and remembered while skippable tours are usually dismissed.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show clear progress through multi-step setup with a checklist or step indicator.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Visible progress and a sense of near-completion motivate users to finish setup.

ux_guidelines.rule: Provide sensible defaults or sample data so users never face an unhelpful blank starting screen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Good defaults and examples reduce blank-page anxiety and show what success looks like.

ux_guidelines.rule: Right-align numeric table columns and keep consistent decimal places and units.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Aligned digits make magnitudes easy to compare at a glance and reduce reading errors.

ux_guidelines.rule: Replace empty data views with an explanation of what belongs there and a clear next action.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Helpful empty states orient new users and turn a dead end into a path forward.

ux_guidelines.rule: Let users sort and filter large data sets and paginate or virtualize long lists.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Interactive controls and chunking keep large datasets usable and performant.

ux_guidelines.rule: Label chart axes, series, and units directly so a chart is understandable without external context.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Self-explanatory charts prevent misreading and reduce dependence on surrounding prose.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show when displayed data was last updated, especially for live or cached metrics.
ux_guidelines.rationale: A freshness indicator lets users judge how much to trust and act on the numbers.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write error messages that state what went wrong and how to fix it in plain language, not codes.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Actionable human-readable errors help users recover instead of getting stuck per Nielsen error recovery.

ux_guidelines.rule: Place each error message next to the field it concerns and associate it programmatically for assistive tech.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Located announced errors let everyone including screen reader users find and fix the exact problem.

ux_guidelines.rule: Prevent errors with input constraints, clear format hints, and confirmation of risky actions before they happen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Stopping mistakes before they occur is more effective than explaining them afterward per Nielsen heuristic five.

ux_guidelines.rule: Preserve the user work after a failure and offer a clear retry rather than forcing a restart.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Protecting in-progress work and enabling retry turns failures into minor speed bumps.

ux_guidelines.rule: Give not-found and system error pages a plain explanation and a clear path back to working content.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Helpful fallback pages keep users from hitting dead ends and abandoning the product.

ux_guidelines.rule: Label buttons with the specific action they perform such as Create account, not generic verbs like Submit.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Action-specific labels set accurate expectations and reduce hesitation at decision points.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write specific situation-aware empty and error text instead of vague generic phrases.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Precise wording tells users exactly what happened and what to do next.

ux_guidelines.rule: Use one consistent term for each concept across the entire interface and documentation.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Consistent vocabulary prevents users from wondering whether two different words mean the same thing.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write in active voice and the everyday language of users, avoiding internal system or developer jargon.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Speaking the language of users makes the product feel approachable and easy to understand per Nielsen heuristic two.

ux_guidelines.rule: Front-load the most meaningful keyword in labels, headings, and menu items.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Leading with the key term improves scannability since users fixate on the first words.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show skeleton placeholders that mirror the final layout for content that takes longer than 500ms to load instead of spinners.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Skeletons reduce perceived wait time and prevent jarring layout shifts once real content arrives.

ux_guidelines.rule: Apply optimistic updates for high-confidence actions and reconcile or roll back gracefully if the server rejects the change.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Immediate visual response makes the interface feel instant while preserving correctness on failure.

ux_guidelines.rule: Validate a field on blur or after a typing pause, not on every keystroke, and never before the user has finished a first attempt.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Premature errors interrupt users mid-thought and feel accusatory, while on-blur timing respects their flow.

ux_guidelines.rule: Surface a clear saving and saved status with a timestamp whenever content persists automatically.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Visible save state reassures users their work is safe and removes the anxiety of losing changes.

ux_guidelines.rule: Offer an undo affordance for reversible actions instead of forcing a confirmation dialog before they happen.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Undo lets users move fast while still recovering from mistakes without modal friction.

ux_guidelines.rule: Require explicit confirmation, ideally typed for high-impact cases, only for irreversible destructive actions and state exactly what will be lost.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Reserving confirmation for truly unrecoverable actions keeps the safeguard meaningful and prevents dialog fatigue.

ux_guidelines.rule: Expose available keyboard shortcuts through a discoverable overlay and show hints next to their corresponding menu items.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Hidden shortcuts only help users who already know them, so visible hints widen adoption and efficiency.

ux_guidelines.rule: Trap keyboard focus within an open modal, return focus to the triggering element on close, and close on Escape.
ux_guidelines.rationale: A proper focus trap keeps keyboard and screen reader users oriented inside the dialog instead of lost behind it.

ux_guidelines.rule: Honor the prefers-reduced-motion setting by removing or substituting large transitions, parallax, and auto-playing motion.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Excessive motion can trigger nausea and vestibular disorders, so respecting the OS preference is an accessibility requirement.

ux_guidelines.rule: Never rely on color alone to convey meaning; pair it with text, icons, patterns, or position.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Roughly one in twelve men cannot distinguish common color pairs, so redundant encoding keeps information accessible.

ux_guidelines.rule: Mirror layout, iconography, and directional gestures for right-to-left languages using logical CSS properties rather than fixed left and right.
ux_guidelines.rationale: RTL users expect a fully reflected interface, and logical properties prevent broken layouts across directions.

ux_guidelines.rule: Format dates, separators, and numerals through locale-aware APIs instead of hardcoding a single regional format.
ux_guidelines.rationale: A date like 03/04 means different days across locales, so localized formatting prevents costly misreadings.

ux_guidelines.rule: Display monetary values with the correct currency symbol, placement, decimal precision, and grouping for the user's locale.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Incorrect currency formatting erodes trust in commerce flows and can cause real financial confusion.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show times in the user's local timezone with an explicit zone label and store all timestamps in UTC.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Ambiguous timestamps cause missed meetings and scheduling errors across distributed teams.

ux_guidelines.rule: Prefer pagination or an explicit load-more control over infinite scroll when users need to find specific items, bookmark positions, or reach the footer.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Infinite scroll buries footers and makes returning to a known item nearly impossible.

ux_guidelines.rule: Keep sticky headers slim or auto-hide them on scroll-down so they do not consume scarce vertical space on small viewports.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Tall persistent headers eat mobile screen real estate and push primary content out of view.

ux_guidelines.rule: Limit breadcrumb trails to a sensible depth and collapse middle levels with a menu when the hierarchy is deep.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Overlong breadcrumbs wrap awkwardly and stop communicating location at a glance.

ux_guidelines.rule: Debounce search-as-you-type queries by roughly 250 to 350ms and cancel stale in-flight requests before issuing a new one.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Debouncing avoids hammering the backend on every keystroke and prevents out-of-order results from flickering.

ux_guidelines.rule: Encode active filters and sort order in the URL so views are shareable, bookmarkable, and survive a page reload.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Losing filter state on refresh or share forces tedious re-selection and breaks collaboration.

ux_guidelines.rule: Support shift-click range selection and a clear select-all-across-pages distinction when offering bulk actions on lists.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Ambiguity between selecting the visible page and the entire result set leads to dangerous accidental batch operations.

ux_guidelines.rule: Provide a keyboard-operable alternative for every drag-and-drop interaction and announce reordering with live region updates.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Pointer-only drag interactions exclude keyboard and screen reader users from core functionality.

ux_guidelines.rule: Auto-dismiss informational toasts after a readable duration scaled to message length and let critical or actionable toasts persist until dismissed.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Toasts that vanish too fast lose their message, while permanent ones for trivial events become clutter.

ux_guidelines.rule: Use a determinate progress bar with steps or percentage for operations longer than a few seconds rather than an indefinite spinner.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Determinate progress sets expectations and reduces abandonment during long-running tasks.

ux_guidelines.rule: Detect loss of connectivity, communicate offline status clearly, and queue or disable actions that require the network.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Silent failures on a dropped connection leave users confused about whether their actions took effect.

ux_guidelines.rule: Warn users before an idle session expires and offer a one-click way to extend it without losing unsaved work.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Abrupt logouts that discard in-progress work are a major source of frustration and lost data.

ux_guidelines.rule: Give real-time strength feedback based on actual resistance to guessing rather than rigid composition rules like forced symbols.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Entropy-based feedback encourages genuinely strong passphrases instead of predictable rule-satisfying patterns.

ux_guidelines.rule: Offer passkeys or platform authenticators as the primary option and keep recovery and fallback factors clearly accessible.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Phishing-resistant passkeys improve security while accessible recovery prevents permanent lockouts.

ux_guidelines.rule: Make rejecting non-essential cookies as easy as accepting them, with equal prominence and no pre-checked boxes.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Asymmetric consent banners are coercive dark patterns and breach privacy regulations.

ux_guidelines.rule: Provide a self-service way for users to export their personal data in a portable, machine-readable format.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Data portability is a legal right under privacy law and builds user trust in your handling of their information.

ux_guidelines.rule: Group related form fields into labeled fieldsets so long forms read as digestible sections rather than an undifferentiated wall.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Logical grouping reduces cognitive load and helps assistive technology convey form structure.

ux_guidelines.rule: Show a step indicator with total count and current position in multi-step flows, and allow returning to completed steps.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Visible progress sets expectations and lowers abandonment in long sequential flows.

ux_guidelines.rule: Prefill fields with safe, context-derived defaults so users confirm rather than type whenever the value can be reasonably inferred.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Sensible defaults cut effort and error rates while still leaving the user in control.

ux_guidelines.rule: Confirm a successful copy with an immediate transient state change on the trigger, such as a checkmark or copied label.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Without confirmation users cannot tell whether the copy worked and often click repeatedly.

ux_guidelines.rule: Use tooltips only for brief non-interactive hints and switch to a popover or dialog when content is interactive or essential.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Interactive or critical content inside hover-only tooltips is unreachable by touch and keyboard users.

ux_guidelines.rule: Keep primary submit buttons enabled and explain validation errors on click instead of silently disabling them.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Disabled buttons give no reason for the block and leave users stuck guessing what is wrong.

ux_guidelines.rule: Use anchors for navigation to a URL and buttons for in-page actions so behavior, keyboard support, and assistive roles stay correct.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Mismatched semantics break new-tab, focus, and screen reader expectations that users rely on.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reveal hidden swipe and long-press gestures with subtle visual cues or a one-time hint rather than leaving them invisible.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Undiscoverable gestures hide functionality from users who never learn the interaction exists.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reserve pull-to-refresh for scrollable list views, give clear pull and release thresholds, and confirm the refresh visually.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Clear thresholds and feedback prevent accidental triggers and confirm the content actually updated.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reserve haptic feedback for meaningful confirmations and errors rather than firing it on routine taps.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Overused haptics become noise, annoy users, and drain battery without adding signal.

ux_guidelines.rule: Avoid pure black backgrounds and pure white text in dark mode, and convey elevation with lighter surfaces instead of heavy shadows.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Maximum contrast in dark themes causes halation and eye strain, especially for astigmatic users.

ux_guidelines.rule: Keep body text at a minimum of 16px on mobile and never disable user zoom to enforce a layout.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Smaller text triggers auto-zoom on focus and disabling zoom strands low-vision users.

ux_guidelines.rule: Constrain body text to roughly 50 to 75 characters per line for comfortable sustained reading.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Lines that are too long make the eye lose its place when returning to the next line.

ux_guidelines.rule: Structure content with descriptive headings, short paragraphs, and front-loaded key points so it can be scanned, not just read.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Most users scan rather than read word for word, so a clear hierarchy surfaces the essentials fast.

ux_guidelines.rule: Write microcopy in a consistent voice that favors plain, human language over jargon and blame-free phrasing for errors.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Consistent, humane microcopy builds trust and reduces confusion at decision points.

ux_guidelines.rule: Abbreviate large numbers for display but expose the full precise value on hover, focus, or tap.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Abbreviation aids scanning while access to exact figures preserves accuracy for decisions.

ux_guidelines.rule: Prioritize columns by importance on narrow screens and progressively hide or stack lower-priority ones rather than forcing horizontal scroll.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Dumping a wide desktop table onto mobile buries the columns that matter most behind awkward scrolling.

ux_guidelines.rule: Label both axes with units, indicate the scale, and disclose whenever an axis does not start at zero.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Unlabeled or truncated axes mislead viewers about the magnitude and meaning of the data.

ux_guidelines.rule: Place legends close to the data and prefer direct in-line labeling over a detached key when series count is small.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Direct labels remove the back-and-forth matching effort that separate legends impose.

ux_guidelines.rule: Cap the number of simultaneously plotted series and aggregate or filter dense data instead of overplotting into illegibility.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Beyond a handful of overlapping series a chart becomes noise that no one can read.

ux_guidelines.rule: Keep UI transitions in the roughly 150 to 300ms range with appropriate easing so motion feels responsive, not sluggish.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Animations that drag past a few hundred milliseconds make the interface feel slow and get in the way.

ux_guidelines.rule: Restore the previous scroll position when users navigate back to a list or feed instead of resetting them to the top.
ux_guidelines.rationale: Losing scroll position on back navigation forces users to re-find where they were and re-scroll through content.

ux_guidelines.rule: Reflect significant view state like open tabs, selected items, and modals in the URL so any view can be linked and reloaded.
ux_guidelines.rationale: State that lives only in memory cannot be shared, bookmarked, or recovered after a refresh.
